claims.text: The as-processed HfNbTaTiZr alloy contains inherent microstructural and compositional heterogeneities.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between heterogeneous regions generates internal residual stresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
These mismatch-generated residual stresses control the thermoelastic and mechanical responses of HfNbTaTiZr.
A homogenization anneal will reduce microstructural and compositional heterogeneity relative to the as-processed state.
Reducing heterogeneity by homogenization will reduce internal residual stresses.
Regions differing in chemical composition and/or short-range order have different thermal-expansion coefficients.
Heating and cooling convert regional thermal-expansion differences into local residual stresses.
Local residual stresses influence dislocation motion and interface behavior.
Residual-stress effects on dislocations and interfaces modulate creep rate, aging-induced hardening, and elastic response.
Homogenized specimens should have lower tensile creep rates at 1250 °C than as-processed specimens.
Homogenized specimens should exhibit less aging-induced hardening at 600–800 °C than as-processed specimens.
Homogenized specimens should exhibit more uniform elastic moduli over 293–1100 K than as-processed specimens.
The relevant response boundaries are elastic-modulus measurements from 293 to 1100 K, aging at 600–800 °C, and tensile creep at 1250 °C.
Mechanisms outside the specified temperatures or under different processing conditions may differ.
The proposed comparison uses identically tested homogenized and as-processed HfNbTaTiZr specimens.
